questionText:

"A state education board implemented a mandatory 'Life Skills Education Program' for 5,000 secondary school students. Surveys prior to the program indicated high adolescent distress: 65% struggled with chronic procrastination, severe exam anxiety, and inability to refuse peer pressure regarding substance experimentation. The curriculum trained students in: (1) Assertiveness training (saying 'No' clearly without aggression or guilt), (2) Time management techniques (prioritizing tasks via the Urgent-Important matrix), (3) Cognitive reframing, and (4) Progressive Muscle Relaxation (PMR) developed by Edmund Jacobson. Post-intervention assessments after six months demonstrated a 50% drop in reported exam anxiety, improved scholastic achievement, and significantly enhanced subjective well-being."
